text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected for function-calling /tools/parse-record in customer VPC 'monarchhealth' (dedicated pool m-pool-12). Error: SchemaMismatchError. Sev: P2. Paging on-call now.

sarah: acked. I'm oncall. taking initial triage. @mike @lee can you join?

mike: on it. I can access the pool metrics. seeing a spike in 5xxs starting around 2025-11-09T02:20:10Z. looks correlated w/ a deploy to model-parse-v3 ~02:18.

ashley: CS reporting multiple customer requests failing with tool-calls in their UI. Customer says ~15-25% of tool calls error with "schema mismatch". they're blocked on some workflows.

jordan: grabbing logs from the tenant router now, pulling recent X-Request-IDs.

lee: from quick look at model logs: new tokenizer/kernel changes in model-parse-v3 introduced stricter output shape enforcement. Some older clients (monarchhealth's parser shim) expect nested `patient` object but engine now emits flat `patient_id` field in some branches. SchemaMismatchError thrown by runtime checker.

sarah: so it's schema drift triggered by model change, causing function-calling parser to reject responses. customer is on dedicated pool so we can do tenant-level mitigations.

mike: proposed mitigations: 1) route monarchhealth traffic to compat-model-v2 (previous model) 2) temporarily disable runtime schema validation for their route 3) rollback model-parse-v3 from m-pool-12 if needed. Which one first?

ashley: customer asks for fastest fix. they prefer no rollback if possible.

lee: fastest safe path = route their traffic to compat-model-v2. no rollback, minimal blast radius. disabling validation would let malformed payloads through -> risky for downstream systems.

jordan: agree. I'll prepare route switch and monitor.

sarah: go for route switch. notify CS and the customer that we're routing them to a compatible model and monitoring for 15m.

mike: executing route change now:
```
redwoodctl route set --tenant monarchhealth --pool m-pool-12 --model compat-model-v2 --reason "mitigate schema-drift after model-parse-v3 deploy"
```

mike: done. API returned 200. CDN invalidation queued.

jordan: verifying... traffic for tenant 'monarchhealth' now hitting compat-model-v2. 2xxs have jumped, error rate dropping from 22% -> 3% in last 60s.

ashley: telling customer: "we've routed your traffic to a compatible model variant (compat-model-v2) while we investigate. This should restore your workflows. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." they replied :thumbsup:.

lee: quick note on root cause: model-parse-v3 output contract changed subtlely in edge branch: nested `patient` -> flattened fields. Our model onboarding validation missed this because unit test prompt set didn't include the older shim responses.

sarah: good. next steps: 1) keep routed to compat-model-v2 for 1h 2) run eval harness comparing model-parse-v2 vs v3 on monarch prompts 3) plan rollback of v3 in pool if evaluation shows widespread mismatch 4) postmortem + change to onboarding tests. owners?

mike: I'll own the routing rollback plan and metrics dash.

lee: I'll run the eval harness & prepare diff report.

jordan: I'll collect logs and sample failed payloads and post a gist.

sam-cs: noted for customer comms and followup. we need ETA to share with MonarchHealth SOC — any privacy/PII risk?

lee: no indications of data exfiltration. Errors occur before downstream handlers accept structured fields; our logs show validation exceptions, stack traces only. redacting already active.

sarah: severity: keep at P2 given partial customer impact but quick mitigation done. We'll escalate to P1 only if routing cannot restore or if wider pools affected.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: routing change applied. Current error rate for tenant monarchhealth: 3.1% (down from 22%).

ashley: CS passing update to customer, they confirmed workflows restored for main flows. Secondary edge-case tools still being validated.

lee: running targeted evaluation now (sample size 200 recent requests from customer). can post results in ~20m.

jordan: uploading logs to internal s3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1765623456-monarchhealth/ (logs redacted).

mike: monitoring CPU/GPU and queue depth on m-pool-12; no resource spikes. route switch looks clean.

sarah: nice work. small action item list:
- lee: eval + diff report (ETA 30m)
- jordan: attach representative failed payload examples to incident thread (ETA 20m)
- mike: keep monitoring + prepare rollback playbook (ETA 1h)
- ashley/sam-cs: update customer with expected timeline and PS contact (ongoing)

sam-cs: acknowledged. will set a follow-up call if anything blocks.

(30m later)

lee: eval done. summary: 200 samples -> 38 cases where v3 produced flattened fields incompatible with the customer's parser shim. attaching small diff in gist: https://gist.internal/redwood/monarch-eval-1765623456 (redacted).

jordan: added 12 failed payload samples to the incident thread.

mike: no regression outside monarchhealth observed in pool after rollout, but we'll keep the rollback plan ready.

ashley: customer says "thank you, things are much better. please keep us posted."

sarah: with mitigation holding, moving to monitoring mode. we'll do a formal postmortem and add onboarding tests to catch shim-like responses.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Owner=sarah, Sev=P2, Start=1765623456, CurrentState=mitigated (routing fallback).

sarah: handing to night oncall @jordan for 23:00 PDT shift handoff. Jordan, please watch for any reappearance and keep CS looped.

jordan: taking handoff. I've got the dashboard pinned and alert thresholds tightened for monarchhealth-specific metrics.

sarah: thanks team. postmortem owner will be lee + mike. target publish within 72h. closing thread for active mitigation; will reopen if customer impact rises. :white_check_mark:
